fields.name: human_position
fields.meaning: position in human RyR1, UniProt P21817-1, sequence version 3; empty where the partner has no human residue

fields.name: human_residue
fields.meaning: the human residue at that position

fields.name: partner_position
fields.meaning: position in the partner's UniProt sequence (rabbit P11716 version 1, mouse E9PZQ0 version 1, pig P16960 version 2); empty where the human residue has no partner

fields.name: partner_residue
fields.meaning: the partner's residue at that position

fields.name: correspondence
fields.meaning: whether the two residues are paired by the alignment

fields.name: indel
fields.meaning: subject-only: a human residue with no partner; object-only: a partner residue with no human residue

fields.name: ambiguous
fields.meaning: true where another alignment of equal score pairs this residue differently, or with nothing

fields.name: reliability
fields.meaning: lowered near an insertion or deletion, in repeats, in disordered or compositionally biased stretches; the reasons are in the mapping table's reliability_reasons

rules: A row whose correspondence is no-correspondence is drawn as a gap, never as a pair.
A residue flagged ambiguous is drawn as such: another alignment of equal score pairs it otherwise.
Reliability is encoded; lowered rows are not hidden.
The caption below is used verbatim.
caption: Human RyR1 residues (UniProt P21817-1, sequence version 3) matched to their partners in rabbit (UniProt P11716, version 1), mouse (E9PZQ0, version 1) and pig (P16960, version 2) RyR1, from ChannelScope's release ryr1_mappings_v0.1. A gap marks a residue with no partner; a residue flagged ambiguous could be paired otherwise by another alignment of equal score; reliability is lowered near insertions and deletions, in repeats, and in disordered or compositionally biased stretches.
